title: unify-credential-wear-leveling-and-stream-signal-bridge-across-py-ts-go
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Multiple SDKs implemented independent credential rotation heuristics and stream-signal APIs which led to subtle token exhaustion races and divergent ergonomic surfaces when consumer code tried to migrate between Python/TS/Go. This work consolidates the runtime-facing credential wear-leveling algorithm and introduces a minimal stream-signal bridge API that is implemented consistently across the three SDKs. Goals: 1) eliminate a class of reauth races observed in long-lived streaming sessions; 2) provide a compact, low-allocation signal/heartbeat contract for pull- and push-style streams; 3) harmonize public ergonomics so client libraries present parity for session leasing and retry windows. Changes: - Introduced a small cred_wear module (algorithm and tunable parameters) with a deterministic state machine for lease renewal backoffs. - Added StreamSignal interface (minimal methods: ping, drain, reopen) and a language-idiomatic bridge implemented in py/ts/go SDK wrappers. - Centralized metrics hooks (signal_sent, reauth_attempt, lease_expiry) and exposed lightweight opt-in telemetry bindings to Redwood Console. - Reworked reauth path so token refresh is attempted proactively when wear threshold is reached rather than reactively on 401s; fallbacks remain for edge cases. - Added comprehensive unit + integration tests that replay recorded long-running stream traces (10k tokens/session) for each SDK binding. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains compatible; new parameters are behind opt-in flags (SDK env var or client option) for gradual rollout. Migration: consumer-facing examples updated in docs/examples/streams to show new ergonomic patterns. Testing & rollout: ran cross-language integration harness in benchmark-lab with representative latency profiles; observed 34% reduction in reauth-induced stream restarts and ~6% lower median tail latency for sustained sessions. Checklist: - [x] API surface design review with DX - [x] Perf runs in benchmark-lab - [x] Telemetry events validated in staging - [x] Docs snippets updated - [x] SDK version bumps prepared for release
